title: Patriot Is Now Streaming on ZEE5. The Mammootty-Mohanlal Reunion That Flopped in Theatres Gets Its Second Life.
excerpt: The spy thriller that earned more overseas than it did at home is now available in five languages across India's fastest-growing OTT platform.
body:
Patriot, the Mahesh Narayanan-directed spy thriller that brought Mammootty and Mohanlal together on screen for the first time in eighteen years, is now streaming on ZEE5. The film went live on the platform on June 5 in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Hindi — barely five weeks after its theatrical release on May 1.

## The Numbers Tell a Peculiar Story

Patriot is one of those rare Indian films that earned significantly more from audiences outside India than inside it. Its opening weekend worldwide gross stood at ₹63.61 crore, but the split was unusual: ₹38.50 crore came from overseas markets, while India contributed just ₹25.11 crore. North America alone delivered $334,000 over the weekend, making it the third-biggest opening day ever for a Malayalam film in the region.

The film's reported budget of ₹125 to ₹140 crore made a profit nearly impossible. Despite crossing ₹80 crore worldwide during its theatrical run, Patriot ended as a commercial disappointment — a box-office miss that was never in question artistically.

## What the Critics Said

The critical reception was mixed but leaning positive. Anandu Suresh of The Indian Express gave it 3 out of 5, praising Narayanan for not being "intimidated by Mammootty and Mohanlal's superstardom" while noting the script "ultimately falls flat." The Hollywood Reporter India called it "a mini miracle" that came close to meeting its sky-high expectations, with Sushin Shyam's score drawing particular praise. India Today's Janani K rated it 3.5 out of 5, calling it "spy cinema done right — minor shortcomings and all."

The consensus among critics was clear: the performances were worthy of the reunion, but the writing could not consistently match the talent on screen.

## Why the Diaspora Angle Matters

The overseas-heavy performance was not accidental. Mammootty and Mohanlal command enormous loyalty among the global Malayalam diaspora, and many NRIs who had not visited a theatre in months made an event of the premiere. The film's themes — a whistleblower narrative about dissent, institutional rot, and patriotic duty — resonated particularly with audiences who are simultaneously invested in India's democratic health and physically removed from it.

With ZEE5 now offering the film in five languages, the diaspora audience that drove its theatrical numbers can revisit it, and a much wider Hindi-speaking audience across India and the Gulf will encounter it for the first time.

## The 18-Year Wait

The last time Mammootty and Mohanlal shared a full-length mainstream feature film was Twenty:20 in 2008. Before that, Fazil's cult classic Harikrishnans in 1998 — famously filmed with two endings to satisfy both stars' fanbases — and the 1989 courtroom drama Irupatham Noottandu stand as high points of a remarkably sparse on-screen partnership.

Patriot's other cast members include Fahadh Faasil and Kunchacko Boban, making it arguably the most stacked Malayalam cast of the year.

## What It Means for ZEE5

For ZEE5, acquiring Patriot is a statement play. The platform already hosted the Manorathangal anthology, which featured both superstars in separate segments. Patriot completes the set — this time, they share the frame. In a streaming landscape where JioHotstar and Netflix are aggressively pursuing South Indian content, landing the year's most anticipated Malayalam film (regardless of its theatrical performance) positions ZEE5 as a serious player in the Mollywood OTT wars.

Patriot did not deliver the blockbuster that the reunion promised at the box office. On ZEE5, free from the pressure of a ₹140-crore breakeven target, it just needs to deliver two superstars doing what only they can do. The reviews suggest it does at least that much.
author: Diaspora Desk
